title: Production acceptance: run Chromium sandboxed as the display user

verify.summary: Fresh independent verification passed source/static kiosk policy checks, but effective pilot-host proof is unavailable: the display account, /usr/bin/chromium, installed service and managed display process are absent. The reachable origin GET returned 200; the checker HEAD 405 is not treated as outage. An unrelated unmanaged Chrome with unsafe flags was observed, not used as proof and not stopped.

TASK-049 still requires a real-machine pilot-host check for its T3 acceptance; that deferred evidence is not a blocker for local feature development or independent local tasks. Source-only GREEN cannot close this task. Resume later in an authorized pilot-host-capable context where the source-managed unit is already installed and running as display, then rerun fresh /verify; do not install, start, stop or restore kiosk Chrome/service as an inferred tactic. Direct dependent TASK-054 remains separately blocked by TASK-046/TASK-052.

Local source-managed kiosk policy and read-only inspection are accepted for the current Linux development phase. Real pilot-host process identity and privilege evidence is deferred until a real server/pilot host exists and is not a current queue gateway.
verify.resume_route: when a real pilot host exists, run the already-defined effective process/privilege check as follow-up acceptance evidence

evidence_required: FT-003-AC-009 RED: no source-managed kiosk execution artifact or focused inspection exists; GREEN: the client-serving Chromium process runs sandboxed without --no-sandbox as the non-privileged autologin display user, whose effective groups/access exclude sudo, Docker and deployment secrets; decisive comparison: scripts/check-kiosk-browser.sh compares effective process UID/command flags and display-user privilege probes against the accepted control without printing profile secrets; artifact: redacted inspection output under .tasks/TASK-049-T3-FT-003-W2/.
purpose: Own only the kiosk browser process identity, sandbox and display-user privilege boundary.
success_outcome: The pilot browser is demonstrably sandboxed and non-privileged under the display user.
anti_goals: Do not implement LNA policy, port topology or automatic restart.
Do not grant the display user any administrative/deployment access.
Do not print browser-profile contents or credentials.

forbidden_scope: LNA/port controls owned by TASK-063 and TASK-065
User-service restart behavior owned by TASK-054-T3-FT-003-W5
stop_conditions: Chromium cannot run sandboxed as display.
Inspection would require revealing profile secrets or changing operator credentials.

constraints: Use source-managed kiosk artifacts and a read-only focused inspection command.
Run on the pilot host without destructive account/group changes.
Retain redacted output under the task directory.
invariants: Chromium runs as display with sandbox intact.
The display user has no sudo, Docker-group or deployment-secret access.
LNA and port claims remain outside this task.
verification_targets: Review of focused source-managed kiosk artifacts and redacted check output.
